name: Food In Literature - Book Club
description:
Food is more than something we eat; it is a record of culture, memory, and the places we come from. In Forgotten Foods, we journey through overlooked ingredients, lost recipes, and disappearing culinary traditions, uncovering the stories and communities behind them. What can rediscovering these forgotten foods teach us about history, identity, and the changing ways we nourish ourselves?
Book of the month: Forgotten Foods.
Edited by Siobhan Lambert-Hurley, Tarana Husain Khan and Claire Chambers
When: Saturday, 26th September, 2026 at 11 a.m.
Where: Atta Galatta Bookstore, Indira Nagar
Ages: 18+
Hosted by: Prachi Grover
Registration is mandatory as we have limited spots.
The session is free & copies of the book are available at the store. 
Prachi Grover is a culinary consultant and educator and is the founder of “From Words to Wok,” a community for people who love to read and eat.

name: Finding the Rhythm in Mundane Life - Dance Workshop
description:
This interactive session, guided by Rajeshwari, offers a sneak peek into how everyday movements can naturally transform into dance.
Dance grants the body and mind a rare chance to discover freedom within structure. Through technique, precision, and poise, Rajeshwari will help participants experience this harmony in a fun, welcoming environment. The workshop is open to all age groups.
Whether you already love to dance or are simply curious about how classical dance training works, come join us and give it a try! 
About the facilitator:
Bharatanatyam has shaped Rajeshwari Aravind’s world for as long as she can remember. What began as a childhood initiation grew into an enduring pursuit marked by constant exploration and refinement.   
Rajeshwari’s approach to dance has always been both expansive and immersive. But her formal training has been multidimensional. 
She has completed a master’s degree in dance at Sastra University, Thanjavur, under Dr Padma Subrahmanyam. She continues her advanced Nattuvangam training with Sheejith Krishna and pursues Carnatic vocal music with Sathish Kumar, Chennai.  For Rajeshwari, dance remains a journey of quiet transformation - one that evolves yet remains a constant pulse of her life.

name: AG Lit Sisters Presents: Our City, That Year - Thematic Book Club
description:
For this month's theme, we're exploring the relationship between literature, identity, and the places we call home.
The reading prompt is simple but fun: members are invited to pick a book with the name of their state in the title. It can be the state they were born in, grew up in, belong to, or have eventually made their home. We'll then come together to discuss the books, our personal associations with these places, and the different ways literature represents them.
As always, readers are welcome and non-readers are celebrated. The meeting is open to anyone who enjoys stories and conversations, whether or not they've completed a book.

name: From the Wild to the Real World - A conversation about wildlife photography, entrepreneurship, risk, failure and finding your own path.
description:
A conversation about wildlife photography, entrepreneurship, risk, failure and finding your own path.
Dinesh's journey into wildlife photography, the stories, challenges and unforgettable moments behind the lens.
Building businesses along the way: the ideas that worked, the ones that didn’t, and what each experience taught him.
What wildlife and entrepreneurship have in common: patience, observation, resilience and knowing when to take the shot.
Buy a copy of Dinesh Kumble’s book, Just Clix!, and have it personally signed by Dinesh.
Limited seats. 
Link in bio.

name: Watercolor Florals - Art Workshop
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta on 26 September for a hands-on watercolour workshop exploring the beauty of loose, flowy floral painting.
We'll begin with a series of painting warmups to get comfortable with the brush, water and pigments. You will then learn techniques for creating beautiful flowers through flowing washes, colour blending and simple shapes, before putting these techniques together to paint your own floral composition.
You can take home all your finished paintings/artworks.
No prior experience is required. All painting materials will be provided, so just come ready to experiment, paint and have fun!

name: BWW Short Story Community - short story community
description:
The BWW Short Fiction Community at Atta Galatta will discuss
The Narayans
By Akhil Sharma
The Narayans by Akhil Sharma is an emotionally precise look at memory, distance, and human connection in an age of digital noise. Set against a sudden break from technology, Sharma’s evocative prose captures how individuals navigate their private inner worlds and attempt to find meaning in simple, low-tech moments.
Read the text and come to the event.

name: Let Poetry Be - Poetry Open Mic
description:
This monthly gathering will see poetry coming to life, through reading, music, art and any other forms of artistic expression, at Atta Galatta. Listeners and performers are all welcome!
Date: 26th September
Time: 4pm
Venue: Atta Galatta, Indiranagar

4. Participants can read to music (acoustic instrument/s), dramatise, use props & costumes

8. The event will begin at 4pm sharp and will be held at Atta Galatta. Participants to report not later than 3:45 pm to hear about performance order and meet the host
9. For any further clarifications, write to us at letpoetrybe@gmail.com
You are now welcome to flood our inbox!

name: The Curse of the Kurus - Book launch
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for the book launch of “The Curse of the Kurus” by Christopher C Doyle. 
Join us for an evening of conversation with the author as we dive into the journey of the book, his research, and the fascinating history behind ancient Indian mythology. Discover how real historical events, Sanskrit texts, and archaeological mysteries inspired this gripping narrative, followed by an interactive Q&A session and book signing.
About the Book
The Curse of the Kurus is the first book in his new Mahabharata: The Itihasa series. Grounded in Sage Vyasa's original Sanskrit shlokas and narrated as itihasa: a record of real historical events, the book explores the origins of the Kuru dynasty, tracking a fateful curse that set off generations of love, sacrifice, high-stakes political intrigue, and revenge.
About the Author
Christopher C. Doyle is an author known for blending ancient Indian mythology, science, and history into fast-paced contemporary thrillers, including popular series like The Mahabharata Quest and The Pataala Prophecy. A graduate of St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, and IIM Calcutta, he brings his extensive research into ancient Indian texts and archaeological legends straight into his writing.

name: Why Do People Buy? - Understading what makes people choose, trust and remember a brand.
description:
Today, people don’t buy simply because something is cheaper or better. We compare, read reviews, ask friends, look things up online, see what others are saying, and increasingly use AI to help us make decisions. What people value is changing too, from price and convenience to health, sustainability, identity and the experience a brand gives them.
In this hands-on workshop, we’ll explore why people choose what they choose and what that means for the brands we build. Through simple activities, discussions and a real-time product evaluation, we’ll look at how people discover products, decide what’s worth paying for, and decide which brands to trust. 
You’ll also examine your own offering and leave with practical ways to make your product, story and messaging more relevant to the people you want to reach. 
Limited seats. 
Link in bio.

name: Children of Heaven - Film Screening
description: Ali has lost his sister Zohre's shoes. They are poor, and need to get the shoes before someone finds out. Ali gets the grand idea of participating in a race to win new shoes for Zohre.

name: Blank Page Club - A workshop for the culturally curious
description:
ave you ever laughed out loud at unexpectedly silly dialogue in a film? Played a song over and over until you knew every note and lyric? Quoted your favourite novel in the caption of your Instagram photo dump? 
This is where writing begins - with paying attention, noticing what connects, and bringing it to meet what you want to say.
Blank Page Club is a writing workshop is for people who love books, films, music, art, memes, or anything else that makes them feel something. We’ll read, listen, share and notice what moves us (and why) in text and other media .and then use those observations to write something that’s entirely our own.
No experience needed. Just bring your curiosity and your opinions.

name: The Nila Festival For the Arts - Audition #3
description:
Nila Festival of Arts, is a multifaceted arts experience for children and parents, celebrating arts and artists with unique offerings and logistics, planned by Atta Galatta for the year 2027. The festival aims to showcase art and culture in a grand pageant that children and parents can participate in and enjoy- art for the sake of art.  To kick off the Festival , we will be holding auditions for Dance Schools at Atta Galatta, to select the final six schools that will be featured in the festival. All performers will be between the ages of 8-16, and would welcome your support.
Join us to support Kalasinchanam Dance School, Padmalaya School of Dance and Nrityanjali school of arts as they audition. Entry is open to all adults and children who would like to watch, support and encourage arts.

name: Read A Kitaab - Book Club
description:
📚 Some books are banned. Some stories are silenced. But conversations can’t be.
Join us for our September Monthly Meet by Read a Kitaab, as we dive into the fascinating world of BANNED BOOKS—the stories that challenged norms, sparked controversy, and refused to stay quiet. 👀📖
🗓️ Sunday, 27th September
⏰ 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM
📍 Atta Galatta, Indira Nagar
🎟️ Entry free | Registration mandatory

name: FLAW TO FLOW 🎨 - A tote-painting experience by Funcovered.
description:
A little paint.
A blank tote.
A few questionable decisions.
And somehow… something beautiful.
Come make, mess up, experiment and see where it takes you.

name: A Storywalk through Indiranagar - Storytelling
description:
On a Saturday morning, walk through the lanes of Indiranagar with Vikram Sridhar to discover the area through its folklore, heritage, and ecology. The walk will begin and end at Atta Galatta. The tales will revolve around historical, mythical, and personal narratives woven as we discover the area through the walk.
Date: 3rd October (Saturday)   
Time: 7 AM
Starting Point: Atta Galatta
Age Group: 16+

name: Once Upon A Brunch - Saturday Morning Meal and Culinary Storytelling
description:
Late weekend morning, brunch, stories like the ones from the olden times, meeting new people
What if they all come together?
Weekend and late-morning brunch is an emotion. On the other hand, stories have always been an emotion too. What's common between the two is the rich heritage of food and stories. What if they come together?
Listen to these stories of the food as you enjoy your weekend Brunch set at a cozy location that has its own stories. A beautiful day starts with a lovely breakfast. And a morning with breakfast and stories. Every food we eat has a story to share... Idli, Vada, bread, paratha, etc. Every breakfast comes after a long break and is eager to be eaten. A simple Weekend morning Brunch put together by Atta Galatta
Culinary storytelling by Vikram Sridhar

name: Earth Tales  - Book Launch
description: Celebrating India’s relationship with nature and the communities that help sustain it, the afternoon will feature a folk music performance, dramatised readings of folktales from across the country, conversations on ecology, and the launch of Earth Tales by the Centre for Contemporary Folklore, published by Duckbill, an imprint of Penguin Random House India. We welcome folklore enthusiasts of all ages!

name: Daughter of the Ocean - A Special Diwali Screening for Kids
description:
A 50-minute animated fantasy adventure inspired by Goddess Lakshmi, the Samudra Manthan, and the timeless story behind Diwali.
Follow young Bhargavi on an extraordinary journey beneath the ocean, filled with adventure, friendship, courage and wonder, as she discovers a destiny far greater than she imagined.
Inspired by India’s rich stories and traditions, Daughter of the Ocean brings an ancient story to life through a completely original animated adventure created for a new generation.
🪔 A special Diwali experience for kids & families
🎬 50-minute animated movie
🌊 Adventure • Fantasy • Indian Stories

name: We Matched, Unfortunately  - Book Lauch
description:
Join us for the launch of We Matched, Unfortunately, a humorous and heartfelt anthology featuring real stories about modern dating, awkward matches, unexpected connections, and everything that happens when romance doesn’t quite go according to plan!
The evening will feature storytelling by the book’s contributors and guests, along with interactive dating-themed games such as Dating Taboo, Do You Know Your Gen Z Dating Terms?, and Dating Bingo. Expect funny stories, lively conversations, prizes, and plenty of relatable dating moments.

name: Where Creativity meets Everyday style - Tote Bag Painting Workshop
description:
Join Bangalore-based artist Angana Phookan for an immersive Tote Bag Painting Workshop on 10 October. Explore colours, patterns, and artistic expression as you design a tote that reflects your personal style. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply looking to try something new, this workshop is for you.
Create something beautiful. Make it uniquely yours.

name: Authentic Relating Games  - Playful yet deep games to help people connect
description:
Ever wonder what is possible when we drop the small talk and connect for real?

Authentic Relating Games is a global practice of guided, playful yet deep exercises (the 'games') designed to help people connect more honestly and meaningfully — whether with close friends or complete strangers.

Through structured partner and group conversations, you will get to practice speaking from the heart, deep listening, and noticing what's alive in you as you relate to others.  The games create space for more honesty, curiosity, and real human connection — often in ways that feel surprisingly fun, refreshing, and profoundly moving.

What to Expect

- A Structured Container:  We will start as a full group to set some simple guidelines that ensure the space feels safe, respectful, and confidential.
- Activities with Partners, Trios, and the Large Group: We'll keep changing partners throughout the session (no need to bring a partner!).
- Guided Prompts and Demos: We'll guide you step-by-step through the games and provide live demonstrations so you know what to do.
- Total Autonomy: You are always in the driver's seat.  You choose how deeply you want to go, or pass on a prompt or game at any time.
- A New Set of Games: If you attended Authentic Relating Games previously, don't worry this won't be the same games but a different set of activities to explore!

No experience needed.  Come as you are.  If you've never done anything like this before, don't worry — it's simple and there is no pressure to get it "right".

About the facilitator:
Roy Jacob is the founder of the Conscious Communication Academy and has been facilitating workshops and retreats for over 15 years, mostly for changemakers as well as team retreats for NGOs and companies.  Roy grew up in the U.S. before finding his calling and coming to India (where his roots are) in 2003.  He believes in the transformative power of combining radical honesty with radical care.
